## Peer-Reviewed Research and Natural-History Notes

::: {.publication-stack}
::: {.publication-entry}
#### Wewhare, N. and Krishnan, A. (2024)

**Individual-specific associations between warble song notes and body movements in budgerigar courtship displays.**  
*Biology Open*, 13(10): bio060497.\
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1242/bio.060497) | [Project summary](../projects/budgerigar-multimodal-courtship.qmd) | [First Person interview](https://journals.biologists.com/bio/article/13/10/bio061701/362431/First-person-Nakul-Wewhare)

Analysis of 100 courtship bouts tests associations between warble-note types and synchronized body movements, identifying population-level and individual-specific coordination patterns.
:::

::: {.publication-entry}
#### Madabhushi, A. J., Wewhare, N., Binwal, P., Agarwal, V., and Krishnan, A. (2023)

**Higher-order dialectic variation and syntactic convergence in the complex warble song of budgerigars.**\
*Journal of Experimental Biology*, 226(20): jeb245678.  
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.245678) | [Project summary](../projects/budgerigar-dialectic-convergence.qmd)

Longitudinal comparison of two budgerigar colonies identifies colony-associated differences in higher-order warble-song structure and convergence following social contact.
:::

::: {.publication-entry}
#### Wewhare, N. and Pandey, U. (2021)

**First record of scavenging by a Checkered keelback, *Fowlea piscator* (Schneider 1799) (Natriciidae) from Western Maharashtra, India.**\
*Reptiles & Amphibians*, 28(2), 348-349.  
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.17161/randa.v28i2.15638)
:::
:::

## Preprints

The manuscripts in this section have not yet been peer reviewed.

::: {.publication-stack}
::: {.publication-entry}
#### Wewhare, N., Burkart, J. M., and Wierucka, K. (2026)

**Sequence-level vocal convergence in common marmosets.**\
*bioRxiv*.\
[Preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.03.20.713272) | [Project summary](../projects/marmoset-vocal-convergence.qmd)

The preprint tests audience-dependent changes in sequence structure and individual phee-call acoustics following pair formation. The manuscript is currently in revision.
:::

::: {.publication-entry}
#### Sarkar, R., Pal, T. S., Maji, S., Nandi, S., Lahiri, A., Basumatary, A. K., GP, A., Wewhare, N., Jahan, N., Jakhete, S., Bandyopadhyay, S., Adhikary, R., Paul, T., Majumdar, S., and Bhadra, A. (2025)

**Sight, smell and more: What cues do free-ranging dogs use for decision-making while scavenging?**\
*arXiv*, 2512.00058.\
[Preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2512.00058) | [Project summary](../projects/free-ranging-dog-decision-making.qmd)

Field choice experiments evaluate how free-ranging dogs integrate visual and olfactory information across alternative food-choice conditions.
:::

::: {.publication-entry}
#### Dhati, A. M., Wewhare, N., Devasthale, N. S., Sundar, S., Parulekar, N., and Krishnan, A. (2025)

**Vocal sequences of diverse parrots suggest an important role for note repetition.**  
*bioRxiv*.  
[Preprint](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.10.24.684295) | [Project summary](../projects/parrot-vocal-sequences.qmd)

Across six parrot species, observed sequence metrics are compared with random, Markov, hidden-Markov, and renewal models; results identify prominent note repetition and support contributions from both renewal- and Markov-like processes.
:::
:::

## Manuscripts and Analyses in Progress

These entries are unpublished and should not be cited as completed publications. They document current analytical scope and are explicitly separated from peer-reviewed and preprint outputs.

::: {.publication-stack}
::: {.publication-entry}
#### Wewhare, N. and Krishnan, A. (in preparation)

**Vocal learning mediates aggressive interactions in budgerigars.**<br>
Unpublished manuscript in final preparation.<br>
[Project and current results](../projects/budgerigar-competition-vocal-structure.qmd)

An observational analysis of associations among male aggression, mutual display, dominance, warble syntax, and learned contact-call repertoires within one mixed-sex colony. Estimates and interpretations may change during manuscript preparation and review.
:::

::: {.publication-entry}
#### Wewhare, N. (analysis in progress)

**Vocal matching and the initiation of vampire-bat exchanges.**<br>
Unpublished PhD research.<br>
[Research theme](../research/themes/vocal-matching/) | [Project and visualizations](../projects/vampire-bat-vocal-matching.qmd)

Preliminary models from Princeton pair recordings and Panama trio recordings test whether acoustic distance from a potential responder's recent calls predicts response probability within five seconds. Playback and behaviour-linked analyses are ongoing.
:::
:::

## Talks and Workshops

- **Evidence that vampire bats use vocal matching to address specific group members**, contributed talk at the *20th International Society for Behavioral Ecology (ISBE)* meeting (Turin, Italy, July 2026; travel-award recipient).
- **Quantifying syntactic convergence in common marmoset vocal sequences**, contributed talk at *Bioacoustics & AI 101: Making AI Accessible to Everybody* (University of Copenhagen, September 2024). [Recording](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bZplC_TDW1M)
- Poster on budgerigar courtship displays at the *5th Conference of the Indian Society of Evolutionary Biologists* (October 2024).
